summary.text: Alexis Toth is remembered as a priest and defender of Orthodoxy in North America. The published life describes his Eastern Catholic background, education, bereavement, and reception into the Orthodox Church, followed by ministry among immigrant communities. It recounts his work in several American cities and the later veneration of his relics at Saint Tikhon's Monastery.

blocks.text: Alexis Toth came from a Carpatho-Russian Eastern Catholic family and was ordained a married priest. He lost both his wife and their child. His work before America included teaching church history and canon law, administration, and responsibility for an orphanage.

blocks.text: Sent to Minneapolis in 1889, Alexis encountered rejection from the Latin-rite bishop John Ireland. He and his parish subsequently sought reception into Orthodoxy. Later he served at Wilkes-Barre and guided other immigrant parishes into the Orthodox Church.
